description: An ESP32-S2 dev board (single-core Xtensa, Wi-Fi only, native USB). Legs are labeled by silkscreen number, not raw GPIO number, except TX/RX (UART0) which keep their named labels.
how_to_use: Peripherals (I2C, SPI, UART) can each be mapped to nearly any GPIO in software (the ESP32's GPIO matrix), so no bus pin is hardware-fixed the way it is on an AVR board — only TX/RX (UART0, used for USB flashing/Serial Monitor unless native USB mode is used instead) are excluded by default. ADC-capable pins for this variant aren't catalogued yet — verify before relying on analogRead-specific substitution.

plain.what: A Wi-Fi board (no Bluetooth) that can also pretend to be a USB keyboard or mouse.
plain.how: Plug in USB and program it like an Arduino. 3.3 V pins.
